title: Meta Funds Seven Gas Plants to Power Biggest Data Center
source_used: KALB (Entergy regulator hearing, 15 Apr 2026); Bloomberg original of 27 Mar 2026 identified via Google News but not readable
key_facts: Bloomberg first reported on 27 Mar 2026 that Meta would fund seven new gas power plants for its Louisiana data center; EnergyNow re-posted that story with a 3 Oct 2026 date and its URL path still reads 2026/03.
Entergy asked the Louisiana Public Service Commission to approve seven new gas plants before the end of 2026 for Meta's planned $27 billion data center in Richland Parish.
Entergy asked to fast-track the review and skip parts of the normal process, including independent analysis meant to protect customers.
The seven plants come on top of three gas plants already approved for the same data center, according to the Alliance for Affordable Energy.
Consumer advocates warn some costs could be shifted to residents and other ratepayers across the state.
On 15 Apr 2026 commissioners approved Entergy's procedural motion 4 to 1; a final vote on the application was set for November 2026.
quote_evidence: Entergy is asking state regulators to approve plans to build seven new gas power plants before the end of 2026 for Meta's planned $27 billion data center in Richland Parish.
"Our concern as a consumer advocate is that some of those costs will be shifted onto residents and other ratepayers across the state."
Commissioners approved the motion from Entergy by a vote of 4 to 1. A final vote on the application is set for November.
why_it_matters_hint: Ten gas plants for one data center, with the cost split still undecided by Louisiana regulators.
